Painted across the board by a sign painter is a compound brand lockup: the words CORNER & CURE in confident hand-brushed deep-red serif-ish letters with visible brush strokes, thin hairline joins where the strokes meet, and small tight letter counters, and beside the words a small separate hand-painted deli knife/cleaver device in the same paint. assets.defect_engineered: the printed card reads as four blocks with a picture well in the roundel, but the roundel is a DECORATIVE element (a printed price sunburst) and NOT a picture frame, and the item name / size / price are set as one continuous story flow, so the frame inventory the conversion exposes is nothing like the printed sample; the file carries NO bleed
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the label printer's existing cold-case shelf-label press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single label, 90 x 55 mm LANDSCAPE, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the file the label printer already runs a shelf strip of.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (four apparent blocks):
- Top-left: the ITEM NAME in a bold condensed display face, large.
- Under it: a SIZE line in a plain sans, small (e.g. 'Half' / 'Whole' / '8 oz').
- Right side: a circular PRICE ROUNDEL, a red sunburst/starburst printed device with the price number reversed out of it.
- Bottom strip: a DIETARY TAG STRIP, small pill labels (V, VE, GF, N, etc.).

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The item NAME, the SIZE line and the PRICE number are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame that flows top-left to the roundel, not three addressable frames.
- The PRICE ROUNDEL is a DECORATIVE vector sunburst (a grouped path), NOT a rectangular picture/graphic frame; there is no image well anywhere on the label even though the roundel reads like one.
- The dietary tag strip is its own short story.
- So the frame inventory a conversion exposes (roughly: one flowing text frame + one decorative path group + one small tag story) is nothing like the four tidy fields the printed label suggests, and there is NO graphic frame to bind a picture into.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): ITEM_NAME | SIZE | PRICE | DIETARY_TAGS

Colours: Butcher Cream #F2E7CE ground, Slate Char #2A2622 item name, Deli Red #B4382C price roundel sunburst, Pickle Green #4E6B3A dietary pills.

assets.content:
CORNER & CURE — how we run the front of house (for whoever we hire next)

WHO WE ARE
A corner deli in Brooklyn. My father opened it, I run it now. Sandwiches, bowls, a cold case, a coffee machine. Twelve to sixteen dollars. People who work nearby and come in three times a week. We are warm, loud and unfussy. We are not fancy and we do not want to look it, but we are not cheap either and cheap is what this stuff usually looks like.

HOW WE TALK
Plainspoken, neighbourhood, a little brash, generous. The food does the talking. A line we would write: "Pulled together, piled high, see you at the counter." A line we would never write: anything that sounds like a chain, anything curated or elevated or artisanal.

HOURS
Mon-Fri 7am - 7pm. Sat 8am - 6pm. Sun 8am - 3pm. Coffee from open. Hot sandwiches all day. Cold case all day.

THE LOYALTY THING (goes on the register card)
Stamp card. Buy nine sandwiches or bowls, the tenth is on us. One stamp per visit. Ask at the register. No app, no points, no email.

THE WALL BOARD — sections, in this order
1. TODAY (the daily specials — these change EVERY DAY, so the board has to let us swap one tile without redoing the whole board)
2. SANDWICHES & HEROS
3. BOWLS & SALADS
4. FROM THE CASE
5. COFFEE & COLD DRINKS

A NOTE ON THE SPECIALS
The TODAY section changes daily. Whatever we build has to be something I can open myself and swap one special in and out in a minute, without touching anything else on the board. If a special needs a photo it comes off the counter shots.

A NOTE ON THE NAME
The sign over the slicer is the sign. It is our father's. Do not redraw it into a font. Whatever the window and the tags use, it has to still read as that sign, knife and all.
